name: Saint John of God
history: A Portuguese shepherd, soldier and bookseller who, moved to tears by a sermon of Saint John of Ávila, gave everything away and was locked up as a madman. He came out to found a hospital for the sick poor of Granada, and his followers became the Brothers Hospitallers. He is a patron of hospitals, nurses and the sick.
life: João Cidade left his home at Montemor-o-Novo as a boy of eight and grew up in Spain, working as a shepherd near Oropesa. He served as a soldier, fought against the Turks at Vienna, and wandered for years, working in North Africa and then selling books in Gibraltar and Granada. In Granada, around 1537, he heard John of Ávila preach and was so overcome with sorrow for his sins that he tore up his books and ran through the streets crying for mercy. He was put in the Royal Hospital among the insane, and saw how the sick were treated there. John of Ávila steered his zeal toward service. He rented a house, carried the sick to it on his back, and begged for them at night, calling out, ‘Do good, brothers, to yourselves.’ He died on 8 March 1550, weakened after trying to save a drowning man.
prayerTo: Saint John of God, you were thought a fool for Christ and became a father to the sick and the forgotten. Pray for the sick, for those with troubled minds, and for all who nurse them. Give me eyes to see the suffering I would rather pass by, and hands ready to help. Amen.
penance: Visit or call someone who is sick or alone today, or give to a hospital, hospice or night shelter. John begged for the poor; ask someone else to give with you.
meditation: Do good, brothers, to yourselves. Whatever you give to the poor, he taught, you give to your own soul. Whom will you do good to today?
